text:
alicia: Quick recap from the GCP negotiation yesterday — they pushed back on a blanket regional availability guarantee. Need to agree on our counter before the redline meeting Tuesday.

mike: TL;DR from their side: they won't commit to 99.9% across every region. Offering continent-level failover and a tiered credit schedule instead.

fiona: That's rough for APAC customers. If we can't get regional SLAs we need explicit carveouts for our top 3 revenue regions or heavier credits.

gcp-sales: Thanks for the summary. To be concrete: we can offer 95% per-region availability for reserved GPU pools, with credits as follows: <95% = 10% monthly credit, <90% = 20% credit. We can also provide cross-region failover assistance and a 6-month ramp on capacity guarantees.

choi: Important: before we take credits we need raw metering exports daily (csv) including instance IDs, preemptible/dedicated flags, and SKU-level billing so finance can reconcile. Is that in scope?

gcp-sales: Metering CSV is doable but typically on a 30‑day rolling export. We can work on tighter cadence for critical customers.

contract-bot: Proposed contract language snippet (from their draft):
```
"Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide 95% availability per Region. Credits are calculated as percentage of monthly reserved fee as shown in Schedule A. Provider liability limited to credits only."
```

alicia: Our counter proposal (high level): 1) 99% availability for our 3 priority regions (us-west1, us-east1, asia-east1) for first 12 months. 2) Safety-stock: provider must maintain an additional 30% buffer of reserved capacity or provide guaranteed prebooked burst capacity. 3) Credits not less than 20% for <99% and 40% for <95%. 4) Daily metering CSV with 7-day dispute window. 5) Right to shift reserved commitments to other providers if sustained shortfall > 30 days.

mike: Addendum: include an escalating remediation playbook — 48h notice to cure, automatic capacity transfer option, and no-penalty termination if unresolved after 90 days.

fiona: I'll run a scenario model: committed spend vs on-demand + credits under 3 failure modes (transient, regional outage, sustained shortfall). Will share numbers by EOD.

operations: FYI our internal telemetry for last 90 days shows ~12% preemption spikes in us-west1 during peak windows; sustained shortages happen for ~4–6 hours, not full days. I'll attach logs to the ticket.

choi: Opening ticket to request daily metering exports and historical preemption data (90d). CC finance and legal.

gcp-sales: We can consider moving to 98% for the top-3 regions and increase the safety-stock to 15% if 7-day metering and a 30-day ramp are acceptable. Also can propose a 30-day disputes SLA.

alicia: Noted. 98% + 15% safety stock is progress but still short of our ask. Legal will want firm language for transfer/shifting rights and invoice-level detail. 

mike: Also pushing that any safety-stock can be either physical capacity or a guaranteed credit-backed commitment for immediate market purchase (i.e., provider pays for third-party burst) — that gives them flexibility.

fiona: For cost context: if they force 15% safety stock we need to quantify who bears the cost — likely baked into committed price. I'll model delta.

alicia: Next steps: Mike to draft redline with the remediation timeline and transfer right by EOD Monday. Choi to get metering + preemption exports. Fiona to share cost sims. @gcp-sales can you return with a written term sheet reflecting the 98%/15% option and a sample credit schedule? :pray:

gcp-sales: Will do — we'll send a revised term sheet by COB Monday.

alicia: Thanks everyone. Keep the thread for updates only.
